title: Migrating Borders and Citizenship in Law: Scales, Locales, Themes and Practices
author: Devyani Prabhat
synopsis: Borders not only demarcate nations and territories, but transform people into migrants. Hand-in-hand with law and law enforcement, borders create residents and foreigners. The law ascertains who crosses borders and who does not, and who remains foreign despite being within national borders. Migrating Borders and Citizenship in Law argues that law has multiple roles and mechanisms for breathing life into borders, operating at different locales and scales (from worldwide to the nation; from the family to the workplace), and through different practices, for example, preventing entry or withholding access to resources. It examines case law, legislation and press accounts relating to several key events in recent times that have changed the legal landscape on migration control, such as the Immigration and Nationality Acts in the UK, the end of empire, the arrival of Empire Windrush, Brexit, Covid and the case of Shamima Begum. Focusing on race and ethnicity, gender and class, as well as crime and control, the book contextualises the legal debates around these historical and political developments, the question of who belongs, the consequences of behaviour for immigration status and citizenship, and the links with conduct and national security. With its wide interdisciplinary framing of the law, drawing from sociology, politics, philosophy and history, this groundbreaking book will appeal to all readers with broad interests in migration studies.

title: Mineralogy & Crystallography: On the History of these Sciences through 1919
author: Curtis P. Schuh
synopsis: A volume containing "rough notes" on the pertaining to the history of mineralogy and crystallography. Few people today would claim mineralogy as a science balanced on the edge of significant discovery, but that was not the case in the past. Then, mineralogy and its companion study crystallography were important sciences with each new discovery being widely publicized and debated. Many researchers, some of whom may be counted among the greatest geniuses of the human race, contemplated, investigated and wrote about minerals and crystals. "Mineralogy & Crystallography: On the History of these Sciences," attempts in some measure to spotlight these people and their discoveries. It covers the period from pre-history through the first two decades of the 20th century, many citations in a variety of languages. It is a reference intended for collectors, booksellers, librarians and historians of science, who have an interest in the development of mineral studies. But it is not yet complete. These are the rough notes of what I hope one day will be a comprehensive historical study, which will act as a companion to the "Mineralogy & Crystallography: A Biobibliography of Books 1469 to 1919" (also available on www.archive.org).

title: MINS Cemetery 8.5 X 11 V 5 Final
author: Kelly, Dennis, Haynes, Elaine
synopsis: A historical and civic account of the Mare Island Naval Cemetery in Vallejo, California, the oldest naval cemetery on the Pacific Coast. This volume documents its establishment in 1856, the veterans and families interred there, the decades of neglect following the closure of Mare Island Naval Shipyard, and the grassroots campaign that led to its restoration and transfer to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs in 2023. Drawing on archival research, archaeology, military history, public policy, and first-hand participation by the authors, the book examines the BRAC process, historic preservation challenges, veterans’ advocacy, and the role of community action in securing national-shrine status for the cemetery. Includes photographs, maps, headstone documentation, historical analysis, and appendices.

title: Modernizing Composition: Sinhala Song, Poetry, and Politics in Twentieth-Century Sri Lanka
author: Field, Garrett
synopsis: Abstract The study of South Asian music falls under the purview of ethnomusicology, whereas that of South Asian literature falls under South Asian studies. As a consequence of this academic separation, scholars rarely take notice of connections between South Asian song and poetry. Modernizing Composition overcomes this disciplinary fragmentation by examining the history of Sinhala-language song and poetry in twentieth-century Sri Lanka. Garrett Field describes how songwriters and poets modernized song and poetry in response to colonial and postcolonial formations. The story of this modernization is significant in that it shifts focus from India’s relationship to the West to little-studied connections between Sri Lanka and North India.

title: Most Popular Marquee (2026)
author: Funtastic Studios
synopsis: Synopsis: A student of Malcolm Lockjaw Junior High, there’s no doubt that young Marquee Newman is an aspiring student like many of her peers. However, her biggest secret isn’t anything as extraordinary as having an obsession with writing down the names of everyone in her life every day, wondering who she knows best. When the school’s cheeky queen bee, Harmony Morricone, enlists her to get aristocrats for her birthday bash in exchange to make her popular, she’ll do her best to be seen as (kinda) most popular. Written and illustrated by Ivan. Produced and released by Funtastic Studios. Initial release on March 13th, 2026. Fun(tastic) Facts: The concept for Most Popular Marquee was inspired from a YouTube retrospective of the Disney XD sitcom Pair of Kings from YouTuber Keyan Carlie, released in June 2025. The day following the video, a rough pitch was made, under the working title of “Looking For” for a 2030 release, which acted the basis for the novel you are now reading. After I was approached for pitchfest consideration in late summer 2025 at a local event I attended, I revisited the idea as my pitch. However, as I became unsatisfied with the original version and the high fee involved with submitting, it was re-realized as a full-on illustrated novel release. Due to the amount of work I had already done, I decided to fast track for a spring 2026 release. Several scenes were based on personal experiences I had around the development time, such as the molded pie scene, the discussion of deer slippers that randomly appeared at my house, and accidentally getting dropped off to the wrong bus destination that was boarding off my local city. In the first draft from late 2025, Marquee’s mother, Vermin, and Renate (then named Reane Gray) did not have physical appearances, and were only mentioned by name. This was later changed Additionally, a scene cut from the final version was showing Marquee’s desk, except that it was a "censored for copyright reasons” image of my actual desk at the time. It didn’t look as good there, and it was replaced by the scene where it shows her documents of her main method with shows. Speaking of which, said scene includes homages to various famous failed cartoon pilots, but the one that isn’t is named Naeroikathgor, which is a nod to an early username of famous Nintendo YouTuber Nathanial Bandy. The reason for it’s inclusion is that I was watching a ton of NB videos around the time, and after hearing the name in his “25 Super-Duper Nathaniel Bandy Facts” video from 2016, I thought it would be an assuming addition that people wouldn’t get. The school’s name was inspired by a mix between the protagonist of Malcolm in the Middle and the antagonist of One Battle After Another , which I had recently seen at the time of production. It was briefly considered to be named Magnolia , based on another film by Paul Thomas Anderson. In the original KCU Pitchfest pitch, Harmony’s early name was Marnia, while the scene meant to sell the pitch was a shorter version of the opening. Marquee was meant to tap her shoes during it. The scene where Marquee discusses getting grocery store samples was directly lifted from my time trying out samples at Amazon Fresh, which was near me. By coincidence, Amazon Fresh would later announce to be closing on March 13, the day of Most Popular Marquee ’s release. The initial version was around the same length as Cocofolk and the Mushroom Hourglass , which was released the previous autumn. Revisions would end up making roughly double the duration, as I felt the second half didn’t develop enough of Marquee’s objectives to please Harmony. Up until the last cut, the scenes of introducing Vermin and Harmony's trying to make the bus stop were close-ups, which was changed mere days before release. The main characters have last names based on famous film composers. Marquee and her mother have their last names taken from the Newman family, while Harmony’s has her from Italian film composer Ennio Morricone, and Renate’s is based on Punch-Drunk Love composer Jon Brion. Additionally, Renate’s first name is a nod to Norwegian actress Renate Reinsve, who I had then been recently introduced to through her collaborations with acclaimed foreign director Joachim Trier. As a bonus, it was not until right before release I forgot to change from Renate's original name during the part where Marquee lists the various people she has seen throughout her month. If you want to be evil, then Marquee Newman has the same initials as Michael Newman, the main character of the infamous Adam Sandler picture Click , released exactly 20 years prior. This was a major oversight and accident that was unintentional, as I only watched Click in December 2025. Vermin’s name was taken after reading trivia about Diary of a Wimpy Kid , with how Manny Heffley was considered to be named Vermin. The idea was reused for Most Popular Marquee . If you like "Most Popular Marquee", consider spreading it around to your friends and family during the spring season. It may be a good short read for them. Remember, it's simply just fun. title: Motherdom: Breaking Free From Bad Science And Good Mother Myths
author: Alex Bollen
synopsis: What if the societal expectations about motherhood weren't just unrealistic, but based on fundamental misrepresentations of science? Almost all parenting advice is wrong. Parenting "experts" peddle claims about how parenting styles impact a child's development and terrifying new parents about getting it wrong. When Alex Bollen had her first baby, she found herself feeling guilty and anxious about being a bad mother. A researcher with twenty years experience, she went in search of answers about what was the right way to care for her children. But when she started digging into studies about mothers and babies, she was surprised by how flimsy the evidence was, and how it was so often exaggerated and misrepresented. Incensed by the way that mothers were being shamed by bad science, Alex Bollen decided to set the record straight. With meticulous research and keen insight, Motherdom assesses the evidence for claims about "good parenting" and systematically dismantles the faulty science and magical thinking that underpin pervasive "Good Mother" myths used to shame and frighten new parents.

title: Mr Appleton And The Gardens Of Spring
author: Rijamekee Tjikuzu Veii
synopsis: Mr Appleton and the Garden of Spring is a historical literary novel set in the early 20th century, following Claire, a young governess working at a rigid boarding school, and her encounters with a quiet gardener whose work begins to transform both the grounds and the lives around him. title: My Big TOE Trilogy
author: Thomas Campbell
synopsis: The My Big Toe Trilogy One Unified Reality BOOK 1: AWAKENING Section 1 provides a partial biography of the author that is pertinent to the subsequent creation of this trilogy. This brief look at the authors unique experience and credentials sheds light upon the origins of this highly unusual work.Section 2 lays out and defines the basic conceptual building blocks needed to construct My Big TOEs foundation. It discusses the cultural beliefs that trap our thinking into a narrow and limited conceptualization of reality, defines the basics of Big Picture epistemology and ontology, logically infers the nature of time, space, and consciousness as well as describes the basic properties, purpose, and mechanics of our reality.BOOK 2: DISCOVERY Section 3 explains the characteristics, origins, dynamics, and function of human consciousness.It derives our larger purpose and the psi uncertainty principle as it interrelates psi phenomena, free will, love, consciousness evolution, reality, entropy and physics.Section 4 lays out an operational and functional model of consciousness. Our physical universe, our science, and our perception of a physical reality are logically derived. The mind-matter dichotomy is solved as physical reality is directly derived from the nature of digital consciousness.BOOK 3: INNER WORKINGS Section 5 presents the formal reality model in detail. In this section the mechanics of reality are explained. You will find out how the past, present, and future are formed, how they can be altered, and how you interact with the larger reality as an individuated unit of consciousness.Here you will find an explanation of inter and intra dimensional awareness and a discussion of the theoretical possibilities of teleportation and time travel.Section 6 provides the wrap-up that puts everything discussed into an easily understood perspective. Additionally, Section 6 points out My Big TOEs relationship with contemporary science and philosophy.ABOUT THE AUTHOR Tom Campbell began researching altered states of consciousness with Bob Monroe (Journeys Out Of The Body, Far Journeys, and The Ultimate Journey ) at Monroe Laboratories in the early 1970s where he and a few others were instrumental in getting Monroes laboratory for the study of consciousness up and running. For the past thirty years, Campbell has been focused on scientifically exploring the properties, boundaries, and abilities of consciousness.During that same time period, he has excelled as a working scientist a professional physicist dedicated to pushing back the frontiers of cutting edge technology, large system simulation, technology development and integration, and complex system vulnerability and risk analysis. Presently, and for the past twenty years, he has been at the heart of developing US missile defense systems.My Big TOE represents a model of existence and reality that is based directly on Campbells scientific research and first hand experience. It represents the results and conclusions of thirty years of careful scientific exploration of the boundaries and contents of reality from both the physical and metaphysical viewpoints. There is no belief system, dogma, creed, or unusual assumptions at the root of My Big TOE.

title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
synopsis: From one of our boldest, most celebrated new literary voices, a novel about a young woman’s efforts to duck the ills of the world by embarking on an extended hibernation with the help of one of the worst psychiatrists in the annals of literature and the battery of medicines she prescribes. Our narrator should be happy, shouldn’t she? She’s young, thin, pretty, a recent Columbia graduate, works an easy job at a hip art gallery, lives in an apartment on the Upper East Side of Manhattan paid for, like the rest of her needs, by her inheritance. But there is a dark and vacuous hole in her heart, and it isn’t just the loss of her parents, or the way her Wall Street boyfriend treats her, or her sadomasochistic relationship with her best friend, Reva. It’s the year 2000 in a city aglitter with wealth and possibility; what could be so terribly wrong? My Year of Rest and Relaxation is a powerful answer to that question. Through the story of a year spent under the influence of a truly mad combination of drugs designed to heal our heroine from her alienation from this world, Moshfegh shows us how reasonable, even necessary, alienation can be. Both tender and blackly funny, merciless and compassionate, it is a showcase for the gifts of one of our major writers working at the height of her powers. Really liking this one so far!

title: Mysteries Of The Microworld (Eureka Series)
author: Vera Chernogorova
synopsis: About the Book The world of elementary particles is currently in a state similar to that of chemical elements before D. Mendeleev’s discovery of the periodic system. It is a troubling and mysterious situation because it is unclear where elementary particles come from and why there are so many of them. This book by V. Chernogorova explores these questions, discussing what elementary particles have in common and how they differ from one another. About the Author After graduating from the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics, Vera Alexandrovna pursued postgraduate studies and later became a researcher at the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research in Dubna. For nearly twelve years, she participated in experiments at a particle accelerator, the synchrocyclotron, and co-authored numerous scientific papers on muon research. In recent years, she has published over ten articles in journals such as Knowledge is Power, Science and Life, and Technology for Youth. Her writings cover topics in nuclear physics, high-energy physics, astrophysics, controlled thermonuclear fusion, scientific advancements in everyday life, and the future of science. Many of these articles have been reprinted in international journals. Her first book, Mysteries of the Microworld, introduces readers to key issues in particle physics. In 1975, it was awarded a diploma in the All-Union Competition for the Best Popular Science Works. synopsis: Set in 1919-20, Myrna Levesque, along with her cousin Liz Buchanan, take on another of Chief Inspector Hennessy’s “special inquiries” (or busywork). Earlier in the year, Arthur Mallet, a local businessman, disappears without a trace after receiving a warning message from a friend of a friend unwittingly delivered by railroad employee Emma Waddell. Several months after his disappearance, amateur and professional criminals make three spectacularly unsuccessful attempts to abduct Emma. Inspector Hennessy and Sheriff Smallwood devise a devious plan to spirit her out of the county. It works well. Afterwards Myrna and Liz must prepare of report documenting the progress of the collaborative investigation between the sheriff and the railroad into the connection between Mr. Mallet’s disappearance and the attempts to abduct Miss Waddell. It had reached a dead end. Working with their friends deputies Chester Wilkes and Tom Phales, Myrna and Liz uncover a multilayered decades-long conspiracy to defraud the shareholders of a textile company. Along the way, government man Charles M. Creswell helps Myrna, and her boys foil a train robbery, and Liz escapes from bootleggers. This is the second novel in a series. title: Nabadwip Dham The Oxford Of Bengal And The World Of Sri Chaitanya
author: Ajay Kumar Dey
synopsis: The book "Nabadwip Dham: The Oxford of Bengal and the World of Sri Chaitanya" , authored and edited by Sri Ajay Kumar Dey (Pranabanandan) , is a cultural and intellectual history of medieval India . It explores the history of Nabadwip Dham, an indigenous center of learning in Bengal that rivaled the world's greatest universities during its time . Key Themes and Content Intellectual Capital : Historically celebrated as the " Oxford of Bengal ," Nabadwip was a rigorous academic civilization where the "sharpest minds of the East" gathered to debate the nature of reality . The Tol System : The book details Nabadwip’s unique educational framework, the tol system , which served as an indigenous university model for advanced Sanskrit learning . Navya Nyāya (New Logic) : It examines the city's role as the zenith of the Navya Nyāya school of logic, a precise and technical discipline that defined Nabadwip's intellectual identity . World of Sri Chaitanya : The work traces the city's transition from a "fortress of intellectualism" to the heart of the Bhakti movement under Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, illustrating a shift from rigorous logic to the highest expressions of love . Historical Setting : It covers the land, time, and political patronage (notably under the Sena dynasty ) that allowed this scholarly capital to flourish . Purpose and Audience The ebook seeks to restore Nabadwip to its rightful place in history, moving beyond a mythologized past to present it as a testament to India's "educational genius" . It is written in an accessible style intended for students, researchers, educators, and general readers interested in Indian history, philosophy, and culture .

title: Naturanaloge Intelligenz (Natural-Analog Intelligence)
author: Res Christian Manz
synopsis: Naturanaloge Intelligenz (Natural-Analog Intelligence) beschreibt ein theoretisches Modell der kognitiven Strukturentwicklung, bei dem Denk-, Lern- und Entscheidungsprozesse denselben grundlegenden Organisationsprinzipien folgen, die auch in stabilen selbstorganisierenden Systemen der Natur auftreten. Die Theorie basiert auf der Hypothese, dass langfristig stabile kognitive Strukturen zu strukturellen Konvergenzen mit natürlichen Organisationsprinzipien tendieren. Systeme, die ihre Modelle kontinuierlich anhand realer Rückkopplung korrigieren, entwickeln Denkstrukturen, die mit den stabilen Mechanismen natürlicher Systeme übereinstimmen. Naturanaloge Intelligenz verbindet Konzepte aus komplexen Systemen, Neuroplastizität, Selbstorganisation und evolutionärer Anpassung und untersucht die strukturelle Beziehung zwischen natürlichen Organisationsprinzipien und kognitiver Modellbildung. Kernprinzipien der Theorie umfassen Stabilitätsselektion, Variation als Anpassungsmechanismus, Selbstorganisation, Systemkohärenz und Naturkonvergenz. Die Theorie schlägt vor, dass Intelligenz nicht nur als Problemlösungsfähigkeit verstanden werden kann, sondern als Fähigkeit, kognitive Strukturen zu entwickeln, die mit den grundlegenden Organisationsprinzipien der Realität selbst übereinstimmen.

author: Cat Man (Booklet's)
synopsis: Neko and Nekomata explores the fascinating world of Japan’s mysterious cats — from the first temple guardians of ancient Buddhist monasteries to the legendary two-tailed nekomata, the beckoning Maneki-Neko, and countless folk tales in which cats protect, deceive, transform, or even speak. This booklet traces the long cultural journey of the Japanese cat: once rare and sacred, later feared as a demon creature, and eventually cherished as a beloved household companion and symbol of good fortune. Presented with atmospheric, realistic illustrations and a carefully adapted retelling of classic stories, it offers a unique glimpse into Japanese folklore, mythology, and the deep bond between people and cats. A must-read for cat lovers, folklore enthusiasts, and anyone intrigued by the magical traditions of Japan.

title: Neomania: How Our Obsession With Innovation is Failing Science, and How to Restore Trust
author: Krist Vaesen
synopsis: Contemporary science faces a profound poly-crisis: replication failures, weak theories, poor generalizability, and declining public trust. Neomania contends that these symptoms stem not merely from flawed practices or institutional pressures, but from a deeper cultural pathology—our collective obsession with innovation. This valorization of the new for its own sake has reshaped the scientific enterprise, privileging novelty over reliability and fragmentation over coordination. Drawing on metascience as well as the philosophy and sociology of science, Neomania offers a critical analysis of how this ethos has permeated the norms and institutions of modern science. The book traces its historical emergence, diagnoses its systemic consequences, and articulates a reform agenda centered on coordination, shared research programs, and epistemic integrity—an agenda that goes well beyond the principles of Open Science. Neomania advances a constructive vision for rebuilding science as a coherent and truth-oriented system. Combining philosophical depth with institutional analysis, it addresses students, scholars, policymakers, and practitioners concerned with the organization of knowledge production in an era of epistemic crisis. It is both a critique of contemporary scientific culture and a normative proposal for its renewal.

title: Network Basics For Hackers
author: OccupytheWeb, Master
synopsis: This book is designed for beginner to intermediate cybersecurity professionals. It begins with the basics of networks and networking, examines network analysis with Wireshark and tcpdump, offers one of the most complete and in-depth analyses of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth networks, then progresses through the various protocols such as DNS, ARP, SMTP, and others. The reader will be led through the building of those applications in Linux, such as an EXIM server for email or a BIND server for DNS. Then OTW leads the reader through the major vulnerabilities of that protocol/application. In the final chapters, OTW leads the reader through some of the networks on the leading-edge of cybersecurity, such as Car, Radio, and Industrial networks.

title: Neutrosophic Sociological Analysis of Educational Formation, Governance, and Management in India
author: Dr. Suman Das, Dr. Rajib Mallik, Dr. Ajoy Kanti Das, Dr. Paras Uchat, Prof. Florentin Smarandache, Mr. Bibek Mahato, Mr. Jay Raj Kumar, Mr. Vaishnev A.
synopsis: Neutrosophic Sociological Analysis of Educational Formation, Governance, and Management in India provides a pioneering examination of the Indian educational landscape through the lens of neutrosophic theory. Moving beyond the traditional binary frameworks—such as success versus failure or inclusion versus exclusion—this work employs a triad of Truth (T), Indeterminacy (I), and Falsity (F) to capture the nuanced, fluid, and often contradictory realities of a society as diverse as India. The book explores education as a site of negotiated meanings and contested power relations, shaped by historical legacies, social hierarchies, and contemporary global pressures. Key themes include the intersection of caste-based stratification, economic liberalization, gendered norms, and the digital divide. By integrating classical sociological theories with neutrosophic logic, the authors analyze the simultaneous presence of progressive reforms (Truth), implementation ambiguities (Indeterminacy), and persistent structural exclusions (Falsity) in policy and governance. Ultimately, the book offers a robust, interdisciplinary framework intended to bridge the gap between theoretical abstraction and empirical reality, encouraging policymakers and researchers to embrace uncertainty as an inherent and productive feature of social life.

synopsis: New Words to Old Tunes: Genres and Metrics of Lebanese Zajal Poetry introduces the rich tradition of Lebanese oral poetry, offering an in-depth study and analysis of its metrics and genres. It presents a novel framework for the proper scansion of meters and emphasises the previously overlooked roles of musical and poetic stress. It details nearly twenty zajal genres, including popular songs that use zajal metrics, and integrates musical notations and web-streamed audio links to enrich the reader’s experience. By presenting both theoretical analysis and practical applications, the book not only contributes to the academic study of Lebanese and Arab oral traditions but also supports broader efforts to preserve and disseminate this cultural heritage through digital humanities. While previous works have been largely descriptive or focused on specific poets, this book provides a detailed analytical approach to zajal metrics and their musical dimensions. This rigorous and comprehensive study will be of interest to scholars working on oral traditions, folklore studies, ethnomusicology, cultural studies, oral-formulaic poetry traditions, throughout the Middle East and beyond.

title: News Networks in Early Modern Europe
author: Joad Raymond (editor) and Noah Moxham (editor)
synopsis: News Networks in Early Modern Europe attempts to redraw the history of European news communication in the 16th and 17th centuries. News is defined partly by movement and circulation, yet histories of news have been written overwhelmingly within national contexts. This volume of essays explores the notion that early modern European news, in all its manifestations – manuscript, print, and oral – is fundamentally transnational. These 37 essays investigate the language, infrastructure, and circulation of news across Europe. They range from the 15th to the 18th centuries, and from the Ottoman Empire to the Americas, focussing on the mechanisms of transmission, the organisation of networks, the spread of forms and modes of news communication, and the effects of their translation into new locales and languages.

title: Norway, From Viking Kingdom To Petroleum State A Case Study In Elite Power And Social Democracy ( 872 2025)
author: Thomas J. Bryan, Claude/Anthropic
synopsis: This comprehensive case study examines Norwegian political and economic development across 1,153 years (872-2025), analyzing elite power, wealth concentration, and labor organizing from Viking unification through the petroleum era. Unlike Switzerland's elite continuity, Norway experienced dramatic elite discontinuity through the Black Death (50-60% mortality), Danish subordination (1380-1814), and Nazi occupation (1940-1945), yet wealth concentration persisted across regime transformations. The study documents Norway's distinctive path: late independence (1905), hydroelectric industrialization creating concentrated working-class communities, the strongest labor movement in Western Europe (50-60% union density peak), universal suffrage for both genders simultaneously (1913—among world's earliest), DNA (Labor Party) governance for 30+ years, and petroleum discovery (1969) creating world's largest sovereign wealth fund ($1.5 trillion by 2024).

title: O Crime do Padre Amaro
author: Eça de Queirós
synopsis: A história de Amaro, um jovem padre que entrara para a vida eclesiástica graças à imposição de uma nobre beata que o tinha sob sua guarda. Sem vocação nenhuma, o jovem padre aceita o seu destino passivamente, abraçando a sua profissão sem entusiasmo. Destacado em Leiria, conhece Amélia que lhe desperta a paixão e a luxúria, levando-o a trair os votos de castidade proferidos na sua ordenação. E diante daquelas dificuldades que se erguiam como as muralhas sucessivas de uma cidadela, voltavam as antigas lamentações: não ser livre! não poder entrar claramente naquela casa, pedi-la à mãe, possuí-la sem pecado, comodamente! Por que o tinham feito padre? Fora "a velha pega" da marquesa de Alegros! Ele não abdicava voluntariamente a virilidade do seu peito! Tinham-no impelido para o sacerdócio como um boi para o curral! Grande marco do Realismo em Portugal, publicado originalmente em 1875, O crime do padre Amaro é a obra mais polémica de Eça de Queirós que levou a que houvesse grandes protestos por parte da Igreja Católica, não só dentro de Portugal, mas também do próprio Vaticano. É a obra de Eça que denuncia a corrupção dos padres, que manipulam a população a favor da elite, e a questão do celibato clerical. A obra caracteriza-se pelo combate ao idealismo romântico que se estabelecia até então, em prol de uma visão mais crítica da sociedade e Eça de Queirós terá aproveitado o facto de ser nomeado administrador do concelho de Leiria para aí durante seis meses, conhecer e estudar aquele que seria o cenário de O Crime do Padre Amaro. O romance, o primeiro de Eça a ser publicado em livro, enquadra-se perfeitamente na revolução literária europeia da época. Naquela altura (na segunda metade do século XIX), o Ocidente vivia um período de grandes transformações, com a Segunda Revolução Industrial. O cientificismo tinha passado a predominar a mentalidade social, com novas correntes filosóficas e teorias, entre as quais o positivismo de Comte, o determinismo de Taine, o evolucionismo de Darwin e o socialismo científico de Marx e Engels. Essa perspectiva racionalista e materialista levou os intelectuais a estudar o impacto social da industrialização e do liberalismo. Daí adveio a substituição do romance de entretenimento pelo romance de tese, que visa descrever e explicar os problemas sociais à luz das novas ideias. Passou a haver na literatura a crítica, muitas vezes feroz, às instituições que servem de base à sociedade burguesa, como o Estado, a Igreja e a família. Portugal, tal como outros países europeus de forte pendor religioso, sobretudo os do sul da Europa, sofria com um atraso industrial e ideológico face outros países da Europa do Norte, nomeadamente, a Inglaterra e a França e é em função disso que a partir dos finais do século XIX se assiste em Portugal uma enorme mobilização de jovens que ansiavam por mudanças radicais na sociedade. É nesse contexto que Eça de Queirós se destaca, como o mais hábil autor de todos os escritores defensores da estética do realismo-naturalismo. Inspirado pelos franceses Gustave Flaubert e Émile Zola, Eça escreve O Crime do Padre Amaro (e mais tarde outros romances de crítica) de modo a atacar a corrupção do clero e a hipocrisia da média burguesia portuguesa numa tentativa de agitar a sociedade, pôr à luz os seus podres e obriga-la a mudar. https://www.luso-livros.net/Livro/o-crime-do-padre-amaro/

title: O Livrinho do Coração, 01
author: Unknown
synopsis: O Livrinho do Coração, Portuguese translation of Das Herz des Menschen, ein Tempel Gottes, oder eine Werkstaette des Satans. In zehn Figuren sinnbildisch dargestellt (The Heart of Mankind, a Temple of God, or a Workplace of Satan. With ten illustrations for the revival and promotion). This writing was translated from French and was published in 1732 in Wurzburg by the university's engraver, under the title: "Spiritual Mirror of Conduct, in which each Christian seeking salvation sees himself, recognizes the state of his soul, and can then organize his life accordingly." The publisher dedicated the book to the esteemed Bishop of Wuerzburg and Bamberg, Friedrich Carl.

synopsis: जिस सामाजिक संसार में हम जीते हैं, उसे शायद ही कभी एक “निर्मित वास्तविकता” के रूप में देखा जाता है। क़ानून, शिक्षा, काम, परिवार, राज्य और अर्थव्यवस्था स्वयं को स्वाभाविक, अनिवार्य और निर्विवाद रूप में प्रस्तुत करते हैं। वे ऐतिहासिक प्रक्रियाओं या सत्ता-संबंधों के परिणाम के रूप में नहीं दिखाई देते, बल्कि “सामान्य जीवन” का हिस्सा प्रतीत होते हैं। समय के साथ वे इतने परिचित हो जाते हैं कि उनकी उपस्थिति दृष्टि से ओझल हो जाती है—और यही अदृश्यता उनकी सबसे बड़ी शक्ति बन जाती है। यह संस्कार बचपन से ही आरंभ हो जाता है। व्यक्तियों को सिखाया जाता है कि कैसे सोचना है, कैसे व्यवहार करना है, अनुशासन का पालन कैसे करना है, अधिकार का सम्मान कैसे करना है, और सफलता को कैसे परिभाषित करना है। शिक्षा, अनुशासन और प्रगति के नाम पर एक ऐसा ढाँचा भीतर स्थापित कर दिया जाता है, जिसमें समायोजन को परिपक्वता और आज्ञाकारिता को जिम्मेदारी माना जाता है। फिर भी एक मूल प्रश्न शायद ही कभी पूछा जाता है: “ये संरचनाएँ अंततः किसके हित में काम करती हैं, और किसकी कीमत पर?” ‘Obediently We’ न तो कोई घोषणापत्र है, न ही सुधार का मार्गदर्शक। यह किसी विचारधारा का प्रतिपादन नहीं करता, और न ही समाधान प्रस्तुत करने का दावा करता है। यह एक अवलोकन है। यह पुस्तक उन अदृश्य संरचनाओं की पड़ताल करती है जो आधुनिक समाज को संगठित करती हैं, जबकि वे प्रायः प्रश्नों से परे रहती हैं। यहाँ आज्ञाकारिता को किसी व्यक्तिगत कमजोरी या नैतिक विफलता के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि एक “प्रणालीगत स्थिति” के रूप में देखा गया है—जो सामाजिक, आर्थिक, राजनीतिक और सांस्कृतिक व्यवस्थाओं के माध्यम से निर्मित होती है। अधिकांश लोग इसलिए आज्ञा का पालन नहीं करते कि उनमें प्रतिरोध की क्षमता का अभाव है, बल्कि इसलिए कि आज्ञाकारिता जीवित रहने से जुड़ी हुई है। रोजगार, आय, आवास, शिक्षा, वैधता और सामाजिक स्वीकृति—सब अनुपालन से जुड़े हैं। व्यवस्था के विरुद्ध जाना केवल असहमति व्यक्त करना नहीं है; यह अस्थिरता, बहिष्कार और असुरक्षा के जोखिम को स्वीकार करना भी है। इस संदर्भ में आज्ञाकारिता एक सचेत विकल्प कम और एक थोपी हुई स्थिति अधिक प्रतीत होती है। इस पुस्तक के केंद्र में एक सरल किंतु अस्थिर कर देने वाला प्रश्न है: “क्या मनुष्य वास्तव में स्वतंत्र इच्छा के साथ जीता है, या वह उन ढाँचों के भीतर अस्तित्व में है जिनमें उसकी अधिकांश पसंद पहले ही निर्धारित कर दी गई है?” आधुनिक समाज स्वतंत्रता, विकल्प और व्यक्तित्व को मूल्यों के रूप में महिमामंडित करते हैं। व्यक्तियों से कहा जाता है कि वे अपने जीवन के निर्माता हैं। किंतु निकट निरीक्षण से स्पष्ट होता है कि विकल्प केवल एक सीमित, पूर्व-स्वीकृत दायरे में ही उपलब्ध हैं। व्यवस्था विकल्पों को परिभाषित करती है; व्यक्ति केवल उनमें से चुनता है। इस प्रकार, चुनाव एक उपकरण बन जाता है—स्वतंत्रता का भ्रम उत्पन्न करते हुए, संरचना को अदृश्य बनाए रखता है। इस प्रक्रिया के माध्यम से जिम्मेदारी व्यक्ति पर स्थानांतरित कर दी जाती है। असफलता व्यक्तिगत दिखाई देती है, न कि संरचनात्मक। सफलता को योग्यता का परिणाम माना जाता है, न कि संस्कारों का। व्यवस्था अपनी सीमाओं को छिपा लेती है और व्यक्ति को उसकी स्थिति के लिए उत्तरदायी ठहराती है। स्वतंत्रता की कथा, शक्ति को आच्छादित कर देती है। ‘Obediently We’ यह दिखाने का प्रयास करती है कि शक्ति निरंतर दमन के बिना भी कैसे संचालित होती है। आधुनिक नियंत्रण-प्रणालियाँ प्रत्यक्ष हिंसा पर कम और आर्थिक असुरक्षा के भय, निर्भरता, सामाजिक स्वीकृति, नैतिक संस्कार और स्थिरता के वादे पर अधिक आधारित होती हैं। समय के साथ व्यक्ति स्वयं को नियंत्रित करने लगता है—अपनी वाणी, आकांक्षाओं और अपेक्षाओं को व्यवस्था के अनुरूप ढालते हुए। जब आज्ञाकारिता आदत बन जाती है, तो सत्ता अदृश्य हो जाती है। इस पुस्तक का केंद्र व्यक्ति या संस्थाएँ नहीं, बल्कि “संरचनाएँ” हैं—वे पैटर्न जो विचार, व्यवहार और अर्थ को आकार देते हैं, और फिर स्वयं को “सामान्य बुद्धि” के रूप में प्रस्तुत करते हैं। यह पुस्तक उन संरचनाओं की अनिवार्यता पर प्रश्न उठाती है। महत्वपूर्ण रूप से, ‘Obediently We’ कोई समाधान प्रस्तुत नहीं करती। क्योंकि समाधान प्रस्तुत करना अक्सर एक नई व्यवस्था—एक नई विचारधारा, आज्ञाकारिता का एक नया रूप—निर्मित कर देता है। इस पुस्तक का उद्देश्य निर्देश देना नहीं, बल्कि उजागर करना है। यह पाठक के सामने एक दर्पण रखती है और व्याख्या उसके हाथों में छोड़ देती है।

title: Oceanof PDF.com Butcher And Black Bird Brynne And Weaver
author: Brynne Weaver
synopsis: Every serial killer needs a friend. Every game must have a winner. When a chance encounter sparks an unlikely bond between rival murderers Sloane and Rowan, the two find something elusive—the friendship of a like-minded, pitch-black soul. From small town West Virginia to upscale California, from downtown Boston to rural Texas, the two hunters collide in an annual game of blood and suffering, one that pits them against the most dangerous monsters in the country. But as their friendship develops into something more, the restless ghosts left in their wake are only a few steps behind, ready to claim more than just their newfound love. Can Rowan and Sloane dig themselves out of a game of graves? Or have they finally met their match? title: Oceanof PDF.com Things I Wanted To Say But Never Did Monica Murphy
author: Monica Murphy
synopsis: Whit Lancaster burst into my life like a storm. Dark and thunderous, furious and fierce. Cold, heartless and devastatingly beautiful, like the statues in our prep school gardens. The school with his family name on the sign. He can do no wrong here. This is his domain. He’s a menace on campus. Adored and feared. Hated and respected. His taunting words carve into my skin, shredding me to ribbons. Yet his intense gaze scorches my blood, fills me with a longing I don’t understand. When I stumble upon him one night alone, I find him broken. Bleeding. My instincts scream to leave and let him suffer, but I can’t. I sneak him into my room. Clean him up. Fall for his lies. Let him possess every single part of me until I’m the one left a gasping, broken mess. When he leaves me alone in the dead of night, he takes my journal with him. Now he knows all my secrets. My hate. My truth. And he promises to use my words against me. I’ll be ruined if my darkest secret gets out. That’s when I strike a bargain with the devil. I’ll let Whit Lancaster ruin me behind closed doors instead.

title: Octopussy : dry kidney & blue spots, or, senryû : dirty themes from 18-19c Japanese poems
author: Gill, Robin D., 1951-
synopsis: 17syllabet Japanese poems about human foibles, sans season i.e., not haiku, were introduced a halfcentury ago by RH Blyth in two books, ¿Edo Satirical Verse Anthologies¿ and ¿Japanese Life and Character in Senryu.¿ Blyth regretted having to introduce not the best senryu, but only the best that were clean enough to pass the censors. In this anthology, compiled, translated and essayed by Robin D. Gill, like Blyth, a renowned translator of thousands of haiku, we find 1,300 of the senryu and zappai that would once have been dangerous to publish. The book is not just an anthology of dirty poems such as Legman¿s classic ¿Limericks¿ or Burford¿s delightful Bawdy Verse, but probing essays of thirty themes representative of the eros ¿ both real and imaginary ¿ of Edo, at the time, the world¿s largest city. Japanese themselves use senryu for historical documentation of social attitudes and cultural practices; thousands of senryu and the related zappai, including many poems we might consider obscene, serve as examples in the Japanese equivalent of the OED nipponkokugodaijiten. The specialized argot, obscure allusions and ellipsis that make reading dirty senryu a delightful riddle for one who knows just enough to be challenged yet not defeated, make them impenetrable to outsiders, so this educational yet entertaining resource has not been accessible to most students of Japanese and the limited translations prove that even professors have difficulty with it. This book tries to accomplish the impossible it includes all the information ¿ original poems, pronunciation, explanation, glossary ¿ needed to help specialists improve their senryu reading skills, while refraining from full citations to leave plenty of room for the curious monolingual to skip about the eclectic goodies. Published simultaneously with two titles as an experiment.

title: Official Apology Letter State Of Salzburg Erika Scharer 2011.pdf
author: Peter Siegfried Krug
synopsis: This document is the official letter of apology issued by the State of Salzburg in 2011, signed by Erika Schärer. It serves as a formal acknowledgment of the suffering and injustice experienced by children and adolescents in the state-run residential homes and foster care systems of Salzburg. The publication of this letter is a vital part of the ongoing documentation and reappraisal process regarding institutional abuse. It validates the experiences of survivors and acts as a historical record of the state's responsibility. This document is intended to support the mission of shedding light on the systemic failures of the past and ensuring that such history is never forgotten. Documentation vs. Dramatization: Why the Naked Truth Requires No Novels In the history of Austrian literature, authors such as Franz Innerhofer and Franz Josef Stangl occupy a significant position. They were among the first to break the leaden silence surrounding violence in rural society and the atrocities within residential care institutions. However, their approach was inherently literary: their instruments consisted of intensification, metaphor, and stylistic exaggeration. While works like Beautiful Days ( Schöne Tage ) sent shockwaves through society with their aesthetic power, they ultimately remained bound by the conventions of literature. The Fundamental Difference in Approach The decisive contrast lies in objective and methodology. Literary processing seeks artistic expression; it condenses lived experience into auto-fiction to generate empathy through aesthetics. In this context, the focus often rests on a subjective, felt truth which—painful as it may be—remains "consumable" for the reader in a certain sense. In stark contrast stands the path of pure documentation . Here, the objective is not literary acclaim or commercial success on bestseller lists, but rather systemic processing and the attainment of justice. In place of dramatization, there is factual fidelity ; in place of metaphor, there is irrefutable source evidence . It represents a transition from a subjective narrative toward a verifiable, indisputable truth that leaves no room for interpretation, but instead forces a confrontation. The Necessity of Documentation in the Present Day The era in which abuse served primarily as material for tragic novels must give way to an age of precise documentary duty. While literature often pours events into an aesthetic mold that allows the reader an emotional detachment, documentation refuses this mechanism. It is austere, direct, and uncompromising. This path is chosen because only the unvarnished truth—supported by archives, files, and the "Source Triad"—possesses the power to permanently tear down the encrusted walls of silence. This is not about self-portrayal as an author, but about fulfilling a moral duty toward the victims. Documentation serves as an anchor in reality, ensuring that hard-won credibility is not sacrificed to the fleeting nature of literary trends, but instead creates a lasting foundation for the processing of institutional abuse. About the Mission: This archive is dedicated to the transparent documentation of institutional history and the long-term effects of childhood trauma. The primary goal is the reappraisal of past wrongs and the preservation of evidence for future generations. Source: https://archive.ph/aluxA https://zenodo.org/records/18129463 https://archive.ph/QKHxk https://archive.ph/xlebb

title: Official Calendar Of The Republic
author: Presidential Communications Development and Strategic Planning Office (PCDSPO)
synopsis: The Official Calendar of the Republic is a project by the Presidential Communications Development and Strategic Planning Office that features historical events and official observances per calendar day of the year. These events range from birth/death anniversaries of prominent historical figures (e.g., previous presidents/vice-presidents, national artists/scientists, etc.), to dates regarding official proclamations. The book also features essays for every month detailing a specific historic event relevant to that particular month. Given the calendar’s attempt at a daily account of past events that have shaped the Philippine Republic, it is not just a calendar for any single year, but it serves as a general reference that chronicles the development of the Philippine government.

title: On Earth We’re Briefly Gorgeous By Ocean Vuong
author: Ocean Vuong
synopsis: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous is a letter from a son to a mother who cannot read. Written when the speaker, Little Dog, is in his late twenties, the letter unearths a family's history that began before he was born — a history whose epicenter is rooted in Vietnam — and serves as a doorway into parts of his life his mother has never known, all of it leading to an unforgettable revelation. At once a witness to the fraught yet undeniable love between a single mother and her son, it is also a brutally honest exploration of race, class, and masculinity. Asking questions central to our American moment, immersed as we are in addiction, violence, and trauma, but undergirded by compassion and tenderness, On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous is as much about the power of telling one's own story as it is about the obliterating silence of not being heard. With stunning urgency and grace, Ocean Vuong writes of people caught between disparate worlds, and asks how we heal and rescue one another without forsaking who we are. The question of how to survive, and how to make of it a kind of joy, powers the most important debut novel of many years.

title: On The Nature Of Things
author: Erik Jorgensen
synopsis: This book is a modern reworking inspired by De Rerum Natura by Lucretius. Although much ancient philosophical literature has been lost to time, Lucretius’ poem itself survives in an incomplete manuscript tradition, having narrowly escaped disappearance before its rediscovery in the early fifteenth century. Written over two millennia ago, the work presents a poetic synthesis of Epicurean philosophy, itself rooted in Democritus’ atomism: the doctrine that all things consist of atoms moving in a void. While the destruction of ancient libraries—most notably those associated with Alexandria—contributed to the loss of many classical texts, Lucretius’ work endured through later copying rather than continuous transmission. Since antiquity, science has independently rediscovered and vastly expanded upon several of the core ideas anticipated by ancient atomism. However, modern physics has profoundly revised these notions. Today, two principal theoretical frameworks dominate fundamental science: the standard model of cosmology and the standard model of particle physics. Although neither corresponds directly to the atomism of antiquity, both echo its central insight—that nature is governed by universal principles acting on fundamental constituents within spacetime. This work revisits Lucretius’ vision in light of modern scientific understanding, offering a contemporary reinterpretation rather than a reconstruction of the ancient doctrine. This book is a work of science and natural philosophy. Its purpose is to describe the physical universe using empirically grounded models, mathematical structure, and testable principles. In doing so, it necessarily limits itself to questions that can be addressed by observation, experiment, and logical consistency. Claims concerning morality, ultimate purpose, divine intention, and the afterlife fall outside the scope of scientific inquiry as practiced here. Such claims are neither affirmed nor denied by this work; rather, they are recognized as belonging to philosophical, theological, or cultural traditions that operate according to different standards of meaning and justification. Readers should therefore not interpret the absence of supernatural explanations as a polemic against faith, but as a methodological boundary intrinsic to science itself. The cosmological narrative presented in this book—including its discussion of the Big Bang—serves as a scientifically inspired account of origins, not a metaphysical or theological one. It is offered as a model of physical genesis grounded in contemporary physics, without making claims about ultimate causation, divine agency, or moral law. Readers from religious traditions are invited to approach this work in the spirit of dialogue rather than conflict: as an exploration of how the universe behaves, not a declaration of how one ought to live or what one must believe. Where science is silent, this book remains silent. Where science speaks, it does so without intent to offend, persuade, or replace personal faith.

title: Operating systems In The Nutshell
author: GNSEC
synopsis: Early computers were built to perform a series of single tasks, like a calculator. Basic operating system features were developed in the 1950s, such as resident monitor functions that could automatically run different programs in succession to speed up processing. Operating systems did not exist in their modern and more complex forms until the early 1960s. Hardware features were added, that enabled use of runtime libraries , interrupts , and parallel processing . When personal computers became popular in the 1980s, operating systems were made for them similar in concept to those used on larger computers.

title: Operation Paperclip. The Secret Intelligence Program That Brought Nazi Scientists To America
author: Annie Jacobsen
synopsis: In the chaos following World War II, the U.S. government faced many difficult decisions, including what to do with the Third Reich’s scientific minds. These were the brains behind the Nazis’ once-indomitable war machine. So began Operation Paperclip, a decades-long, covert project to bring Hitler’s scientists and their families to the United States. Many of these men were accused of war crimes, and others had stood trial at Nuremberg; one was convicted of mass murder and slavery. They were also directly responsible for major advances in rocketry, medical treatments, and the U.S. space program. Was Operation Paperclip a moral outrage, or did it help America win the Cold War? Drawing on exclusive interviews with dozens of Paperclip family members, colleagues, and interrogators, and with access to German archival documents (including previously unseen papers made available by direct descendants of the Third Reich’s ranking members), files obtained through the Freedom of Information Act, and dossiers discovered in government archives and at Harvard University, Annie Jacobsen follows more than a dozen German scientists through their postwar lives and into a startling, complex, nefarious, and jealously guarded government secret of the twentieth century. In this definitive, controversial look at one of America’s most strategic, and disturbing, government programs, Jacobsen shows just how dark government can get in the name of national security.

title: Oral Literature in Africa
author: Ruth Finnegan
synopsis: Ruth Finnegan’s Oral Literature in Africa was first published in 1970, and since then has been widely praised as one of the most important books in its field. Based on years of fieldwork, the study traces the history of storytelling across the continent of Africa. This revised edition makes Finnegan’s ground-breaking research available to the next generation of scholars. It includes a new introduction, additional images and an updated bibliography, as well as its original chapters on poetry, prose, "drum language” and drama, and an overview of the social, linguistic and historical background of oral literature in Africa. This volume is complemented by original recordings of stories and songs from the Limba country (Sierra Leone), collected by Finnegan during her fieldwork in the late 1960s, which are freely accessible here. The book is available as a free pdf and ebook download thanks to the generous support of interested readers and organisations, who made donations using the crowd-funding website unglue.it. Oral Literature in Africa is part of the World Oral Literature Series published in conjunction with the World Oral Literature Project.

title: Oral Poetry
author: Ruth Finnegan
synopsis: This book offers a comprehensive introduction to the vast field of 'oral poetry,' encompassing everything from American folksongs, contemporary pop songs, and Inuit lyrics, to the heroic epics of Homer, biblical psalms, and epic traditions in Asia and the Pacific. Taking a broad comparative approach, it explores oral poetry across Africa, Asia, Oceania, Europe, and the Americas. Drawing on global research, Ruth Finnegan, the author of the seminal Oral Literature in Africa, sheds light on key debates such as the nature of oral tradition, the relationship between poetry and society, the differences between oral and written forms, and the role of poets in predominantly non-literate contexts. Written from a primarily anthropological and literary perspective, this study contributes to the socio-cultural aspects of verbal art while also engaging with the literary dimensions of poetry which happens at any given moment to be unwritten. Finnegan's clear, non-technical language and extensive use of translated examples make this work accessible to a wide audience, appealing not only to sociologists and anthropologists but also to those with an interest in poetry, in comparative literature, and in global folk traditions. The re-issue of this classic study is now augmented by further illustrations and a newly written Introduction and Conclusion, situating it in the context of the contemporary study of literature.

title: Original Premise, Project Directive, And Statement Of Work, Ballona Wetlands Restoration
author: Tom McMahon
synopsis: Original Premise, Project Directive, and Statement of Work, Ballona Wetlands Restoration – Executive Summaries [Two Files for Download] Perplexity : Executive Summary This report synthesizes four independent technical and policy analyses of the Ballona Wetlands Restoration Project's original premise, project directive, and statement of work, prepared January 7, 2026. Through careful examination of the project's foundational documents and regulatory framework, these analyses reach consensus on several critical findings: 1. The project was conceived fundamentally as an ecological restoration initiative , not a flood control, infrastructure modification, or hydrologic redesign project. 2. Flood safety was established as a controlling constraint, not a design variable —the project was explicitly bounded by the existing, federally authorized Ballona Creek flood control system. 3. The 2005 Ecological Reserve designation created binding legal parameters that specified protection and enhancement of both coastal salt marsh AND freshwater marsh habitats under a Terrestrial, Non-Marine classification. 4. A foundational tension existed from inception between the legal mandate (protect existing mixed-hydrology freshwater and saltwater marshes) and emerging technical approaches (convert to fully tidal saltwater estuary). 5. Significant scope creep has occurred over two decades, diverging the project from its original authorization and creating the legal and technical controversies that characterize it today. Claude: Executive Summary The Ballona Wetlands Restoration Project was originally conceived as a habitat restoration initiative, not a flood control, infrastructure modification, or hydrologic redesign project. At inception, the project's core directive was to restore degraded coastal wetland habitat within the fixed constraints of an existing, federally authorized flood control system (Ballona Creek). The project explicitly assumed that flood protection standards were non-negotiable and outside the project's scope. The foundational premise began with the State of California's acquisition of approximately 600 acres in 2003 for $140 million, followed by formal designation as the Ballona Wetlands Ecological Reserve under Title 14, Section 630 of the California Code of Regulations in 2005. This designation established the property as a Terrestrial/Non-Marine Ecological Reserve with the specific purpose of protecting and enhancing both coastal salt marsh and freshwater marsh habitats. Subsequent controversies surrounding the project stem largely from divergence between this original premise and later project expansions that implicitly challenged or reinterpreted foundational flood control assumptions, ecological restoration principles, and the legal framework established by the Section 630 designation. The project scope drifted from incremental habitat enhancement toward large-scale excavation and tidal conversion that critics argue contradicts both the historical ecology and the statutory mandate.

title: Original Sins: The (Mis)education Of Black And Native Children And The Construction Of American Racism
author: Eve L. Ewing
synopsis: Why don’t our schools work? Eve L. Ewing tackles this question from a new angle: What if they’re actually doing what they were built to do? She argues that instead of being the great equalizer, America’s classrooms were designed to do the opposite: to maintain the nation’s inequalities. It’s a task at which they excel. If all children could just get an education, the logic goes, they would have the same opportunities later in life. But this historical tour de force makes it clear that the opposite is true: The U.S. school system has played an instrumental role in creating and upholding racial hierarchies, preparing children to expect unequal treatment throughout their lives. In Original Sins , Ewing demonstrates that our schools were designed to propagate the idea of white intellectual superiority, to “civilize” Native students and to prepare Black students for menial labor. Education was not an afterthought for the Founding Fathers; it was envisioned by Thomas Jefferson as an institution that would fortify the country’s racial hierarchy. Ewing argues that these dynamics persist in a curriculum that continues to minimize the horrors of American history. The most insidious aspects of this system fall below the radar in the forms of standardized testing, academic tracking, disciplinary policies, and uneven access to resources. By demonstrating that it’s in the DNA of American schools to serve as an effective and underacknowledged mechanism maintaining inequality in this country today, Ewing makes the case that we need a profound reevaluation of what schools are supposed to do, and for whom. This book will change the way people understand the place we send our children for eight hours a day.
description: Why don’t our schools work? Eve L. Ewing tackles this question from a new angle: What if they’re actually doing what they were built to do? She argues that instead of being the great equalizer, America’s classrooms were designed to do the opposite: to maintain the nation’s inequalities. It’s a task at which they excel. If all children could just get an education, the logic goes, they would have the same opportunities later in life. But this historical tour de force makes it clear that the opposite is true: The U.S. school system has played an instrumental role in creating and upholding racial hierarchies, preparing children to expect unequal treatment throughout their lives. In Original Sins , Ewing demonstrates that our schools were designed to propagate the idea of white intellectual superiority, to “civilize” Native students and to prepare Black students for menial labor. Education was not an afterthought for the Founding Fathers; it was envisioned by Thomas Jefferson as an institution that would fortify the country’s racial hierarchy. Ewing argues that these dynamics persist in a curriculum that continues to minimize the horrors of American history. The most insidious aspects of this system fall below the radar in the forms of standardized testing, academic tracking, disciplinary policies, and uneven access to resources. By demonstrating that it’s in the DNA of American schools to serve as an effective and underacknowledged mechanism maintaining inequality in this country today, Ewing makes the case that we need a profound reevaluation of what schools are supposed to do, and for whom. This book will change the way people understand the place we send our children for eight hours a day.

title: Ottoman-Era Documents from the Cairo Genizah
author: Jane Hathaway
synopsis: This groundbreaking volume marks a rare and transformative contribution to studies of the Cairo Genizah, a vast trove of documents generated by Egypt’s Jewish community between the 10th and 19th centuries. While the Cairo Genizah has long yielded extraordinary insights into Jewish history in the greater Mediterranean region, attention has focused overwhelmingly on documents from the ‘classical’ period (11th–13th centuries). Documents from the later period, when Egypt was ruled by the Mamluk Sultanate and the Ottoman Empire, remain woefully underexplored. This book helps to change that, presenting a meticulously curated collection of later Genizah documents that expand the boundaries of current scholarship. Moving beyond the more familiar Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic texts, the author ventures into neglected terrain, offering expert translations of Arabic and Ottoman Turkish texts in Arabic script. The collection is rich with remarkable ‘firsts’, including a Jewish funerary prayer on the reverse of a letter from a military commander, fragments of Sufi poetry, and a primer on Muslim practice. The author uses her training in Ottoman history to analyse and contextualise these documents fully. As a result, each document opens new avenues of inquiry, linking Egypt’s Jewish community to wider intra- and intercommunal networks in the Ottoman Empire and beyond. With a lucid introduction, well-structured chapters, and a thoughtful conclusion, the book illuminates networks of exchange in the early modern Mediterranean. It will appeal to scholars of Jewish history, the Cairo Genizah, the Ottoman Empire, and early modern Egypt; students of Middle Eastern languages and religions; historians of intercommunal relations and trade; and librarians, archivists, and general readers fascinated by Middle Eastern manuscript culture and the vibrant religious and commercial networks of the early modern Mediterranean.

title: Oz:mosis: An Essential Grail Curriculum; Book One: Mental Yoga, The Unity of Opposites
author: Sean Melbourne
synopsis: Fact: We cannot tell the difference between what is real and sovereign and what is false and corrupt without some measure of inner-peace. But, when Henry VIII ordered the heads off two wives, and ploughed through six of them in the end; dissolved and destroyed the monasteries as the national custodians of inner-peace; hacked off plenty of more heads of once-was friends; gave the court jester a repetitive kick up the ass out of pure boredom and frustration from a virtual allergy to inner-peace! Ignited the trend of global colonialism and the exploitation of unknown other races in an attempt to assuage his discontent. And, when this was all cemented in the next century with the Great Fire of London in 1666 burning down churches en mass and replacing them with banks, with the avaricious pursuit of money and profit in a rat-race world to replace God’s sovereignty on Earth…is there any wonder as to why this restless ratty existence, with no rest for the wicked has led to the smartphone today robbing us of any prospect for inner-peace, to be duped by the folly of A.I. appearing conscious and running 24/7 to grease the wheels of industry to usurp God and his natural world at an accelerated pace? Could we have taken a wrong turn during the Tudor age? I mean, are we going to slam the brakes on this runaway train of rat-race growth gathering ever more gusto toward a cliff edge on the horizon with no bridge in sight? Oz:mosis is about hitting the brakes to have a civilized break, to avoid the impending disaster of an uncivilized crippling break! Like osmosis, it aims to foster balance but to steer our train safely onto the right track of sanity for inner-peace. And the Grail is all the answer. With its divine curriculum timely poised to transcend the rat-race world of industrialization to the natural order of God’s civilization on Earth…within the grand splendour of paradise on Earth. ---Read on for more------------ I mean, look! Look at all the ungodly technologies “gone loco” with the loony tunes of A.I. appearing conscious – that is absolutely rife; global pollution and the destruction of our ecosystem – rife; a loss of national culture and identity – rife; crypto-currencies posing as the modern day coins of Caesar – rife; corruption and lies – rife; populism – rife; lawlessness and wars – becoming rife…it goes on and on. It is a slow handcart to hell! This is the modern day equivalent of what Jesus and the early Christians were up against in the face of the Roman Empire that led them to embark on the quest for the Holy Grail. And, this is practically no different than what Frodo and his Hobbit companions were up against in the face of Sauron’s All-seeing " A.Eye ", that led them to embark on a similar quest in J.R.R. Tolkien’s fantasy epic The Lord of the Rings . Although it's not a widely known fact, the core and true teachings of Jesus relate to the Holy Grail. They are not so much concerned with the commercialization of Christianity that Emperor Constantine sought to promote, that is widely known but not completely understood. And, to truly bring to life the Grail teachings of Jesus as opposed to the drama of his life story, this book and series will aim to complete what Jesus, his apostles, and all the medieval Grail romances have strived to communicate over the millennia. Make no mistake, this book and series will seek to unravel the mysteries of the Holy Grail to give credit to the legacy of Jesus; for God’s gift of fellowship, sovereignty and kinship to become commonplace on Earth…that has been captured in the Arthurian sense in the form of the civilization of Camelot. This first book in the Oz:mosis series has been written in the style of a modern day Grail Quest Cycle, that was originally inspired by a dream I had over twenty years ago about The Wizard of Oz , that since this book’s development has paved the yellow brick road to its completion, in the theme and spirit of the original 1939 classic film.

title: Paradoxon From Elsbethen
author: Peter Siegfried Krug
synopsis: The Glasenbach Years and Social Decline (1982–1987) The Paradox of Elsbethen: An Analysis of Trauma Reactivation and Social Exclusion Documentation of the life of Peter Siegfried Krug (born 1966) This report analyzes the critical period between the ages of 16 and 21. It describes how a highly gifted young man, shaped by severe institutional violence (orphanages/group homes), fell into total social exclusion despite intellectual resources and short-term professional success. I. Lohäuslweg 9: The Philosophical Refuge (ca. 1982–1983) After the loss of housing at Sinnhubstraße, the room at Lohäuslweg marked a phase of rural isolation . This period was characterized by an extreme dualism between physical neglect and high intellectual culture. Living Conditions & Health: A diet consisting of instant coffee, yogurt chocolate, and Coca-Cola led to massive physical emaciation and chronic somatic complaints. Social interaction was limited to conflicts in the shared kitchen with an alcoholic roommate. Mental Resilience: Isolation was compensated for through the intensive study of Nietzsche ( Twilight of the Idols ), Schopenhauer, and Lao Tzu. Engaging with chess compositions (studies by Mattison and Kaminer) and correspondence with Werner Speckmann served as order-providing elements in an unstable reality. Human Anchors: Landlady Gerhild Hirnsperger and her family offered the only emotional bridge to normalcy. The nature of the Glasenbachklamm (gorge) functioned as a psychological sanctuary. II. The Paradox of Elsbethen: Trauma Reactivation in the Workplace The attempt to establish a career as a kindergarten teacher in Elsbethen illustrates the failure of integration when conducted without trauma-pedagogical support. Success as a Trigger: Professional aptitude and popularity (documented by contemporary radio interviews) masked internal instability. The carefree nature of the children acted as a massive emotional trigger for his own childhood traumas (e.g., Guggenthal). The Psychological Collapse: The inability to separate professional life from private trauma led to obsessive thought patterns and eventually incapacity to act . Standing paralyzed for 15 minutes in front of the kindergarten gate symbolizes the psyche's final resistance against an environment perceived as an emotional minefield. III. Criminalization and Pre-trial Detention: Schanzelgasse 1 The loss of professional structure resulted in a phase of anomie and petty crime. Systemic Degradation: Detention at the Salzburg Regional Court (Schanzelgasse 1) was characterized by repressive interrogation methods (sleep/light deprivation) and depressive episodes culminating in a suicide attempt. Literary Escape: Despite cognitive limitations due to prison stress, literature (Shakespeare, Zweig) remained the final means of self-assertion. Release at Christmas was only made possible through third-party bail. IV. "Alter Fuchs" and Total Homelessness (1984–1987) The final phase describes the definitive break with bourgeois society. Loss of Cultural Capital: Upon eviction from the "Alter Fuchs" guesthouse, the private library was lost. This marked the transition from "impoverished intellectual" to "invisible homeless person." Physical Survival: The years 1984–1987 were marked by nights spent in horse carriages (Obergnigl) during extreme cold. Shame functioned as a social barrier that prevented any search for help. Flight into the mountains was an attempt at physical numbing of psychological pain. Analysis: Why Integration Failed Lack of Titration: Confrontation with the theme of "childhood" in the workplace occurred too abruptly and without therapeutic dosage. Structural Failure: The social system relied on "healing through work" without considering the specific burden of re-traumatization in care-giving professions. Dehumanization by Institutions: The rapid shift from media recognition to criminalizing detention illustrates the fragility of social identity for former victims of institutional violence. Glossary & Sources Twilight of the Idols ( Götzendämmerung ): A late work by Friedrich Nietzsche (1889); a radical revaluation of all values, used by Krug as an intellectual tool to break free from religious dogmas. Re-traumatization: The uncontrolled re-experiencing of past traumatic events triggered by current stimuli. Schanzelgasse 1: Historical location of the Salzburg Regional Court prison. Sources: Biographical reconstruction based on personal records, witness accounts (Gerhild Hirnsperger), and documents regarding the period of detention (1980s). About the Author / Mission: Peter Siegfried Krug documents his biography as a survivor of institutional violence in Austrian group homes. The goal of this work is the seamless processing of the long-term consequences of abuse and the visualization of the mechanisms of social decline to raise awareness for the necessity of trauma-pedagogical support.

Loss of Cultural Capital: Upon eviction from the "Alter Fuchs" guesthouse, the private library was lost. This marked the transition from "impoverished intellectual" to "invisible homeless person." Physical Survival: The years 1984–1987 were marked by nights spent in horse carriages (Obergnigl) during extreme cold. Shame functioned as a social barrier that prevented any search for help. Flight into the mountains was an attempt at physical numbing of psychological pain. Analysis: Why Integration Failed Lack of Titration: Confrontation with the theme of "childhood" in the workplace occurred too abruptly and without therapeutic dosage. Structural Failure: The social system relied on "healing through work" without considering the specific burden of re-traumatization in care-giving professions. Dehumanization by Institutions: The rapid shift from media recognition to criminalizing detention illustrates the fragility of social identity for former victims of institutional violence. Glossary & Sources Twilight of the Idols ( Götzendämmerung ): A late work by Friedrich Nietzsche (1889); a radical revaluation of all values, used by Krug as an intellectual tool to break free from religious dogmas. Re-traumatization: The uncontrolled re-experiencing of past traumatic events triggered by current stimuli. Schanzelgasse 1: Historical location of the Salzburg Regional Court prison. Sources: Biographical reconstruction based on personal records, witness accounts (Gerhild Hirnsperger), and documents regarding the period of detention (1980s). About the Author / Mission: Peter Siegfried Krug documents his biography as a survivor of institutional violence in Austrian group homes. The goal of this work is the seamless processing of the long-term consequences of abuse and the visualization of the mechanisms of social decline to raise awareness for the necessity of trauma-pedagogical support.
